newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia Yield Spreads-Contract on wage verdict.
newsitem.headline: Australia Yield Spreads-Contract on wage verdict.

text.p: Australian bond yields contracted sharply against the dollar bloc following the "living wage" verdict, reversing Monday's widening bias.

The Australian Industrial Relations Commission (AIRC) granted a A$10 per week pay award, a result at the lower end of market economists' expectated range, and is seen having minimal impact on future wage inflation, analysts said.
The local market had been anticipating a moderate outcome and also remains buoyed on the expectation that Wednesday's March quarter CPI will be benign.

Forecasts centre on a headline CPI rise of just 0.1 percent for the March quarter, bringing the annual inflation rate to 1.2 percent, while the policy-sensitive underlying rate is seen up 0.4 percent for year-on-year growth of 2.1 percent, according to a Reuters survey of economists.

The Australian/U.S. 10-year bond yield spread was closing in on last week's lows, while the contraction at the short-end was more notable as fears of a tightening by the Reserve Bank this year evaporated and there is even some talk of an easing.
In sharp contrast, the U.S. Federal Reserve is expected to tighten policy again, even as early as next month's Federal Open Market Committee meeting.
The U.S. is facing a thin calender for major data this week, but does see note auctions for two and five year maturities, which weighed on U.S. debt in New York and Tokyo.
